Contributing to rsconnect

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

rsconnect is an R package. It deploys content to Posit Connect, Posit Connect Cloud, and shinyapps.io. This guide tells you how to work on the package and which conventions to follow.

Development commands

Run these commands from the package root.

devtools::load_all()          # load the package for interactive work
devtools::test()              # run all tests
devtools::test(filter = "deployApp")  # run tests/testthat/test-deployApp.R
devtools::document()          # update man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen comments
devtools::check()             # run R CMD check
lintr::lint_package()         # run the linters that CI runs

Format the code with air before you commit. CI runs air format . on each pull request and suggests changes if the code is not formatted:

air format .

roxygen generates man/ and NAMESPACE. Do not edit these files manually. Change the roxygen comments and run devtools::document(). CI runs roxygen and fails if man/ or NAMESPACE is not up to date.

CI runs lintr and fails if it finds a problem. The lintr configuration is in .lintr.R, and it needs lintr 3.2.0 or later. The configuration includes two custom linters. One linter finds objects that a test-*.R file assigns at the top level. The other linter finds assignments of an if block with braces. The sections below explain these two rules.

Client objects and S3 methods

Each server type has a client class: connectClient, connectCloudClient, and shinyAppsClient. clientForAccount() in R/client.R makes the correct client for an account.

If a function works with more than one client type, make it an S3 generic. Put the generic in R/client-generics.R and put each method in the file for its client (R/client-connect.R, R/client-connectCloud.R, or R/client-shinyapps.R). Mark each method with #' @export and run devtools::document() so that NAMESPACE registers it. Do not write branching logic on the server type or server name (for example, if (isShinyappsServer(...))) to select the behavior. Add a method instead.

All clients also have the class rsconnectClient. A method for rsconnectClient is the default for all clients, and a method for one client class overrides it. findContentByName.rsconnectClient() is an example.

If a function works with only one client type, do not make a generic. Write a standard function in the file for that client, and validate the client at the start of the function with checkConnectClient(), checkConnectCloudClient(), or checkShinyappsClient():

connectCloudGetContent <- function(client, contentId) {
  checkConnectCloudClient(client)
  ...
}

Code that the RStudio IDE calls

The RStudio IDE calls exported functions and also some internal functions with rsconnect:::. The calls are in SessionRSConnect.R in the RStudio repository. The internal functions are:

  • validateServerUrl(), getAppById(), getUserFromRawToken(), registerUserToken(), and showRstudioSourceMarkers() in R/ide.R
  • isConnectServer(), isPositConnectCloudServer(), and connectCloudUrls() in R/servers.R
  • clientForAccount() in R/client.R
  • getAuthToken() in R/accounts.R
  • hasLint() in R/lint.R
  • cli_menu() in R/utils-cli.R

The IDE also calls some fields on the client objects, for example client$getEnvVars() on the Connect client and client$getContent() on the Connect Cloud client. Do not rename or remove these functions or fields, and do not change their arguments or return values. Before you change an internal function, search SessionRSConnect.R for it, because this list can become out of date. The tests in tests/testthat/test-ide.R call these functions and fields in the same way as the IDE.

Errors and messages

Use cli::cli_abort() for errors, not stop(). If a helper function signals the error for its caller, give the helper a call = caller_env() argument and pass call to cli_abort().

Make sure that each message is correct for all callers. For example, an error in shared code must not name Connect Cloud if the code also runs for shinyapps.io. A message in code that writeManifest() also uses must not talk about deployment.

Tests

Tests use testthat. New tests should go into a tests/testthat/test-*.R file whose name matches the .R file in which the function you are testing is defined. Put all test helpers and shared test data in a tests/testthat/helper*.R file. Do not define them in a test-*.R file. Each test_that() block must run alone after devtools::load_all(), so do not make a test depend on objects that other tests in the same file create.

Before you write a new helper, look for one in the helper*.R files. Some helpers that tests use frequently:

  • local_temp_config() uses a temporary config directory, so that tests do not change the real accounts and servers.
  • local_temp_app() makes a temporary app directory from a list of files.
  • fake_client() makes a client object of a given class.

Use withr to make temporary changes in a test, for example withr::local_tempdir(), withr::local_envvar(), and withr::local_options(). withr undoes the change when the test ends. Write files in a temporary directory, not in the tests/testthat directory.

When you fix a bug, write a failing test first.

Make assertions specific. Do not only check that a call succeeds or fails. Check the values that the code produces, for example the request body or the URL that the code sends.

Integration tests are in tests/integration and tests/shinyapps-integration. They need live servers and run in CI, not with devtools::test().

Code style

Do not assign the result of a multi-line if block to a variable. Assign the variable inside the block. It is usually best to initialize the variable before the block and then overwrite it in the block, so that the variable always has a value. You can also assign the variable in each branch. If the logic is complex, move it into a helper function that returns the value. A one-line x <- if (a) b else c without braces is acceptable.

# Do not do this
plumberInfo <- if (appMode == "api") {
  inferPlumberInfo(appDir)
} else {
  NULL
}

# Do this
plumberInfo <- NULL
if (appMode == "api") {
  plumberInfo <- inferPlumberInfo(appDir)
}

A function must not use variables from the calling environment. Pass all values as arguments.

Avoid <<- as much as possible. It is acceptable in test mocks that record calls. Some package code also uses it. For example, withTokenRefreshRetry() in the Connect Cloud client uses <<- to keep a refreshed token in the authInfo of the client, so that later requests use the new token. In new code, use a different design if you can. Use <<- only if the alternative is much worse.

Look for an existing helper before you write new logic. If the same logic occurs in more than one place, move it into a helper function.

NEWS

Add an entry to NEWS.md for changes that users can see. Write the entry for users. Describe the behavior that changed, not the internal implementation. Put code in backticks. End the entry with the issue number, for example (#1292). If there is no issue, use the PR number.
